_README: TEMPLATE -- every value below is a placeholder. Nothing here was inferred from
your CV, because the CV lives outside this repo and its path has not been given.
This file is what the LLM stage matches job requirements against. profile.json
holds only HARD constraints (geography, seniority ceiling, excluded titles);
it says nothing about what you can do, so the rubric has nothing to work with
Write capabilities as ATOMS: one concrete, evidenced thing you have built or
operated. The rubric asks the model to name a specific atom as evidence for
each JD requirement, and it is instructed to reject vague evidence -- so
'Python' is a weak atom and 'built a RAG pipeline over Postgres + pgvector
serving ~50 QPS' is a strong one. Specificity here directly raises the

identity.current_role: PLACEHOLDER: e.g. QA Engineer at WellnessLiving
identity.career_identity_statement: PLACEHOLDER: the one-paragraph statement from spec.md -- who you are professionally and what you are moving toward.
identity.two_year_goal: PLACEHOLDER: used for trajectory_fit. e.g. 'AI engineer building agentic systems at a product company that hires remotely.'

capabilities.atom: PLACEHOLDER: e.g. Built an LLM job-filtering pipeline: multi-source ingestion, deterministic geo classification, LLM rubric with quote-audited scoring
capabilities.evidence: PLACEHOLDER: where this is demonstrable -- repo, production system, or work project
capabilities.depth: built | operated in production | prototyped | studied

strong: PLACEHOLDER: languages/tools you would be comfortable being interviewed on
working: PLACEHOLDER: things you can be productive in with docs open
exposure: PLACEHOLDER: touched, would not claim in an interview

domain_experience: PLACEHOLDER: e.g. fitness/wellness SaaS, QA automation, LLM tooling
known_gaps: PLACEHOLDER: be honest here. Stating gaps makes the model's interview_odds and
strongest_objection far more useful, and stops it crediting fit you do not have.
